asset.name: Tether USD
asset.contractIs: Tether's own TetherToken (Solidity 0.4.17), not a proxy: the address holds the token code itself. `deprecate(address)` makes it forward every call to another contract.
asset.admin: owner() = 0xC6CDE7C39eB2f0F0095F41570af89eFC2C1Ea828 (a contract; its signers were not examined): blacklist and destroy funds of a blacklisted address, pause, set a transfer fee below 20 bps and below 50 USDT per transfer, issue, redeem, deprecate.

behaviour.transferFee: switch `basisPointsRate` / `maximumFee`, both zero today; the sender loses the amount, the recipient receives it less the fee
behaviour.blocklist: `transfer` checks the sender, `transferFrom` checks `from` only: a blacklisted address still RECEIVES; its balance can then be destroyed by the issuer
behaviour.upgrade: `deprecate(address)`: calls are forwarded to the new contract; balances are read from it

verified.source: https://tether.to/en/supported-protocols/ (Tether's own page names this contract; fetched by agent 409 on 2026-11-18, sha256 c88c040a99d2b04e...)

loopback fork of Ethereum at block 26446459 (public fork source ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com, read-only): code keccak, decimals, owner, transfer / transferFrom / blacklist / pause / fee behaviour with the vault in each role

fee.collection: accrued in the vault outside the backing; anyone calls sweepFees() and the vault pays the recipient
fee.networkFee: the depositor pays the deposit transaction; the relayer pays the release transaction, up to 2 gwei: while the network's gas price is above that the release waits

finality.rule: A deposit is attested when its block is at or below the block the signer's own Ethereum node reports as finalized (two epochs of Ethereum's own consensus).
finality.reorg: Signers read only finalized blocks; a deposit that leaves the canonical chain before finality is never attested. Every mint waits 12 hours on the L2; the relayer does not execute a mint whose deposit is not in the vault's finalized deposit chain and the guardians cancel it. A credited mint with no deposit holds later releases instead of paying them.

deposit.recipientEncoding: bytes32: the 20-byte L2 address left-padded with zeros
steps: read allowance(owner, vault) on the USDT contract; if it is neither zero nor already enough, send approve(vault, 0) first: this token reverts an approve from a non-zero allowance to a non-zero value; then approve the vault for the amount
approve and transfer on this token return no data: do not decode a boolean from them
call deposit(amount, l2Recipient) on the vault
after source finality and the 12 hour mint delay the L2 token credits amount less 0.05% to l2Recipient
refusals: an amount below minDeposit or above maxDeposit, or one that would pass the cap
an l2Recipient that is zero or longer than 20 bytes
do not name a contract as l2Recipient unless it can move the token

a deposit while the asset contract is not in the pinned state (issuer fee, pause, replaced or upgraded token, vault blocked): the vault or the token refuses it, and the signers attest nothing for the route until the state is back

notes: a recipient the issuer has blocked is still PAID by this token (only the sender side is checked); the issuer can then destroy that balance. The burn names the recipient and cannot be redirected
the relayer pays at most 2 gwei per gas: while the network's gas price is above that ceiling a release waits (it is not lost) and is paid when the price falls
the smallest exit is l2MinBurn (100); the fee of an exit covers the relayer's gas only up to a gas price that grows with the amount (docs/BRIDGE-EVM-NETWORKS.md section 9.1)
if the issuer turns its transfer fee on, a release still pays: the vault sends the amount less the bridge fee and the recipient receives it less the issuer's fee (below 20 bps, below 50 USDT)
